title: Draw Better Than Win?!
summary: Sacrifice the queen, underpromote with check, then use the king to trap the opposing king for a knight mate.

nodes.question: How can the advanced pawn rescue this queen ending?
nodes.explanation: White has Kh7, Qa4, d7 and a2 against Kf6, Qb7 and a3. A checking sacrifice can turn the d-pawn into a knight fork.

branches.title: Follow the king and build the knight mate
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece board. This branch verifies the board play, without adopting the narration’s separate claim about clock adjudication.
Qf4+ checks the king while setting up the queen sacrifice.
Ke7 approaches the d-pawn, as illustrated in the source.
Qf7+ offers the queen with check.
Kxf7 takes the queen but steps onto the knight’s promotion fork.
d8=N+ promotes with check and attacks Qb7 at the same time.
Kf6+ escapes the knight check and uncovers Qb7’s seventh-rank check against Kh7.
Nxb7 captures the queen, answers that discovered check and leaves a knight ending with one pawn each.
Ke5 heads toward the last white pawn on a2.
Kg6 follows with the king instead of sending the knight down alone.
Kd4 continues toward the a-pawn.
Kf5 keeps the king close enough to later trap Black near a1.
Kc3 approaches a2.
Ke4 maintains the pursuit.
Kb2 prepares to take a2.
Kd3 approaches the key c2 square.
Kxa2 takes the pawn, but that capture does not make this exact knight-versus-pawn position drawn.
Kc2 traps the king near the a-file. Black’s own a3 pawn limits its king’s exits.
Ka1 retreats to the corner.
Nc5 brings the knight toward the mating squares while Kc2 holds b1/b2/b3.
Ka2 uses the available waiting square.
Nd3 improves the knight while preserving the cage.
Ka1 returns to the corner.
Nc1 controls a2 and threatens Nb3 mate once the pawn moves.
a2 is Black’s only legal move in this board position.
Nb3# is actual mate. The black pawn blocks a2 while the king and knight cover every remaining flight.
branches.explanation: Nb3# is actual mate. The black pawn blocks a2 while the king and knight cover every remaining flight.

branches.title: Promote to a queen after the sacrifice
commentary: Compare the source’s warning against ordinary queen promotion.
Qf4+ starts the checking sequence.
Ke7 approaches the pawn.
Qf7+ offers the queen.
Kxf7 accepts the sacrifice.
d8=Q gives up the win. Unlike the knight promotion, it does not force a reply with check.
Qh1+ checks down the h-file and starts a forced mating finish. Contrary to the narration, this move alone is not mate: Qh4 can interpose.
Qh4 is White’s only legal answer, blocking the h-file check with the new queen.
Qxh4# captures the interposing queen and delivers actual mate. This forced completion is independently supplied beyond the source’s mate-in-one claim.
branches.classification: source setup with independently verified forcing completion after ...Qh1+
branches.explanation: Qxh4# captures the interposing queen and delivers actual mate. This forced completion is independently supplied beyond the source’s mate-in-one claim.

branches.title: Send the knight instead of following with the king
commentary: Compare the source’s attempt to defend a2 with the knight alone.
Qf4+ starts the sacrifice sequence.
Ke7 approaches the pawn.
Qf7+ offers the queen with check.
Kxf7 takes White’s sacrificed queen and steps onto the promotion fork.
d8=N+ forks king and queen.
Kf6+ escapes the knight check and uncovers Qb7’s seventh-rank check against Kh7.
Nxb7 captures the queen, answers that discovered check and leaves a knight ending with one pawn each.
Ke5 begins the march toward a2.
Nc5 sends the knight down but leaves White’s king too far away to build the cage.
Kd4 keeps approaching a2.
Nb3+ checks Kd4 while trying to defend the pawn with the knight.
Kc3 attacks Nb3 and approaches a2 simultaneously.
Nc1 retreats while still guarding a2.
Kb2 attacks the knight on c1 and threatens the pawn.
Nd3+ checks Kb2 and saves the knight, but abandons the pawn.
Kxa2 removes a2. With White’s king stranded on h7, this exact knight-versus-pawn ending is drawn, unlike the main king-pursuit branch.
branches.explanation: Kxa2 removes a2. With White’s king stranded on h7, this exact knight-versus-pawn ending is drawn, unlike the main king-pursuit branch.

exercises.answer: The knight checks Kf7 and attacks Qb7, forcing Black to answer before launching the mating attack down the h-file.

exercises.prompt: Why follow with the king instead of the knight?
exercises.answer: The king must reach c2 to hold b1, b2 and b3. Black’s own a-pawn then traps its king long enough for the knight to deliver mate.

startContext: Begin from the complete seven-piece source root. The verified lesson concerns legal board play and exact tablebase outcomes. The narration’s time-expiration claim is outside this verification: no time control, platform rule or clock adjudication is encoded or certified.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
sourceCorrections: The title and narration include a claim about drawing by time expiration. That claim has not been verified for a specific platform/time control and is not taught here. The encoded board continuation ends in actual Nb3 mate.

The source calls ...Qh1 mate after d8=Q. In the exact saved board it is check: White has the single legal interposition Qh4, followed by ...Qxh4 mate. That forced completion is independently verified here.
